items.followUp: What is the resolving power of an electron microscope?

rubric.why: Magnification is defined as the ratio of image size to the actual size of the object.
rubric.description: Defines magnification as the ratio of image size to actual object size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the correct ratio.

rubric.why: The electron microscope has a magnification power of up to 250,000 times.
rubric.description: Gives the magnification power of an electron microscope.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct value.

modelAnswer: Magnification is the ratio of the size of an image to the actual size of the object.
An electron microscope can magnify an object up to 250,000 times.

items.followUp: How does meiosis help maintain chromosome number and produce variation?

rubric.why: Meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes, so fertilisation restores the usual number and maintains it across generations.
rubric.description: Explains how meiosis maintains chromosome number across generations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes or maintains the chromosome number after fertilisation.

rubric.why: Meiosis generates variation through processes such as crossing over and independent assortment.
rubric.description: States that meiosis produces genetic variation or names a process that produces it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for genetic variation, crossing over, or independent assortment.

modelAnswer: Meiosis halves the chromosome number in gametes, maintaining the chromosome number of a species after fertilisation.
It produces genetic variation through crossing over and independent assortment.

items.followUp: Why do prokaryotes reproduce without meiosis?

rubric.why: Prokaryotes lack a true nucleus, unlike the cells in which meiosis takes place.
rubric.description: States that prokaryotes do not have a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the absence of a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Meiosis involves pairing and separation of homologous chromosomes; prokaryotes do not have homologous chromosome pairs.
rubric.description: Explains that prokaryotes lack the chromosome pairing needed for meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they lack homologous chromosome pairs or have a single circular chromosome.

modelAnswer: They lack homologous chromosome pairs, which are needed for meiosis.
